summary.text:
Small district with a £92.815m PWLB book at 31 December 2025 (GF £41.201m at 2.63% weighted across 8 individually named loans, HRA £51.614m at 2.70% as one aggregated line), and a Capital Financing Requirement of £114.1m at 31 March 2025 rising to £166.9m by 31 March 2029 as the HRA CFR alone grows from £67.5m to £120.6m. The balance-sheet identity ties to the pound at year-end: CFR £114.1m less external borrowing £92.8m less zero other long-term liabilities equals £21.3m internal borrowing, which is the paper's own 'CFR not funded by borrowing' line in Table 1.

The strategy is Tandridge's last as an independent authority. Paragraphs 1.5 and 1.6 state plainly that the Council's borrowing, investments and CFR will consolidate into a new East Surrey unitary from 1 April 2027; capital investment decisions from 2027/28 will be for the new authority to consider. The plan sets £18.5m of new borrowing for 2026/27 before that date, with a further £52m indicative across 2027/28 and 2028/29 for the incoming unitary. The maturity profile carries 55.7% of debt in the over-20-year band against a 60% ceiling.

The reconciliation ties exactly on the General Fund: 8 loans, £41,201,078, 2.63% weighted, matching the paper's Appendix A page 2 line by line, including four loans that mirror the on-lending to Gryllus Property Ltd. The HRA is aggregated in the paper so cannot be reconciled loan-by-loan; our 13 HRA-implied loans sum £52.964m against their £51.614m — an £1.35m gap we cannot resolve without their loan-level detail, so the HRA figure does not go in the email. Arlingclose's Annex 2 quotes the PWLB HRA rate at gilt yield plus 0.40% — 40 basis points below the certainty rate — which is worth flagging against the HRA borrowing profile.

officer.body:
Hi Joe,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 20 January Capital, Investment and Treasury Management Strategy bundle. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

The first thing to say is that your General Fund loan book ties to our file exactly. Companion paper Appendix A shows eight named loans totalling £41,201,078 at a weighted 2.63%, and we hold the same eight — Gryllus Loan, Village Health Club, the two Linden House loans, the two Quadrant House loans, Gryllus 80-84 Station Road and Gryllus Castlefield — line by line and pound for pound, with each rate matching to two decimals. The HRA sits in a single aggregated £51,614,000 line at 2.70% in the same table, so we can't do the same drill-down on that side, but the total reconciliation on the GF is the strongest tie we've had this month.

The reason we looked twice is Annex 2 of your Appendix D. Arlingclose prints the spread structure verbatim: standard rate gilt plus 1.00%, certainty gilt plus 0.80%, HRA gilt plus 0.40%, National Wealth Fund gilt plus 0.40%. The HRA rate is 40 basis points below the certainty rate — the cheapest sterling long-term debt available to any UK borrower, and one only HRA councils can draw. Your Table 4 shows HRA CFR growing from £67.5m at 31 March 2025 to £120.6m by 31 March 2029, and the HRA external debt line in Table 1 tracks the same shape — £51.6m rising to £104.7m — so the roughly £53m of net new HRA borrowing across the plan is exactly the debt that qualifies for that rate. We publish the HRA rate at both fixings each day and hold twelve months of history for the 40bp differential itself, at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

The other observation, which cuts across everything else, is that this is your last independent strategy. Paragraphs 1.5 and 1.6 are unusually direct — the borrowing, investments and CFR consolidate into East Surrey unitary from 1 April 2027, and capital investment decisions from 2027/28 are for the new authority. That puts a clock on the £18.5m of new borrowing planned in 2026/27 (yours to draw) against the further £22m of Total Debt increase indicative for 2027/28 and 2028/29 (theirs to decide, per Table 1 page 34). Of the councils we've read, Cumberland is the only one now three years post-reorganisation, and their MRP policy still runs under five different regimes at once because each predecessor's rules travelled with its debt. Whatever you draw before April 2027 will travel the same way.

One last piece of market context for whoever picks this up next. Bank Rate is 3.75% and Arlingclose's own central case (your Annex 2, 22 December) has it at 3.25% by mid-2026. Twenty-year gilt was 5.16% at the forecast date; the certainty rate off that is 5.96%, the HRA rate 5.56%. Their forecast puts the twenty-year at 4.90% through most of 2026-27, so HRA around 5.30%. If any of the £18.5m gets drawn short of a maturity view, we run the daily curve at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis and publish the sector's monthly draws at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — July saw £368m from 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%.

On the academy: four courses fit Tandridge squarely — Liability benchmark and internal borrowing, which is the shape of Table 2 in your Appendix D; HRA financing and the PWLB HRA rate, which is the 40bp point above; Devolution and reorganisation: the treasury view, written for exactly the position you're planning under; and PWLB break costs — mechanics and live calculator, which is the engine we referred to at the start. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you find any of it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Sources: Capital, Investment and Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 (Appendices A-D) and the Summary Investment and Borrowing Position at 31 December 2025 with its own Appendix A, all Investment Sub Committee, 20 January 2026.
